assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology from the discovery of GLP-1 and its insulinotropic action to receptor-agonist drugs that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits. Originality, clarity of mechanism and breadth of impact on medicine are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion) and Drucker (GLP-2/GLP-1 biology, receptor pharmacology, translation) are central; Mojsov identified the active GLP-1(7-36) form. Knudsen's drug development is decisive for clinical translation but the credit split among academic discoverers and industrial developers is unresolved; Habener's role is, to my knowledge, not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism replicated extensively and large randomized outcome trials confirm benefit; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among physiologists, peptide chemists and industrial developers is contested.
Which of the four credited names is best left out is a judgement; I have not independently verified priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new class of living drugs with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. A clear conceptual and clinical breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June developed the costimulatory CAR designs leading to clinical efficacy; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified lymphocyte therapy. Other early CAR designers (e.g. Eshhar) are not on the credited list, which limits fairness.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation; long-term remission data maturing; solid-tumor application still limited.
uncertainties: Omission of other foundational contributors from the credited names.
Toxicity and limits in solid tumors may affect how the prize is framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically targeted light control of excitable cells has become a foundational tool for causally dissecting neural circuits, including the motor and other circuits I work on. Methodological impact across neuroscience is enormous, though it is a tool rather than a disease mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification (Nagel, Bamberg, Hegemann) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth), plus Miesenboeck's earlier genetic photoactivation, make a three-person limit hard; any trio leaves out decisive contributors.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for two decades; timely and mature as a technology; clinical translation is early (vision restoration).
uncertainties: Credit allocation among six names is difficult and contentious.
Relative weight of tool-building versus disease impact in the committee's view is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic discovery of SMN2 exon 7 splicing control led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a fatal infant disease into a treatable one and establishing antisense therapeutics. Clear discovery-to-patient arc.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and target sequence and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development; the two-person configuration is clean. Contributions of other SMN2 and splicing researchers may be underweighted.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up and independent confirmation; recognition timely.
uncertainties: Whether the Prize panel prefers earlier SMN1 gene identification credit not on this list.
Antisense chemistry priority relative to earlier oligonucleotide pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VLP-based HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level evidence of dramatic declines in precancer and cancer. Major public-health impact following zur Hausen's recognized discovery.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs; Frazer contributed to VLP vaccine work and early development. Others (e.g. Zhou, Kirnbauer) are not credited, so the trio is a reasonable but imperfect configuration.
assessment.maturity: Real-world effectiveness data over more than a decade confirm efficacy; timely.
uncertainties: Dispute over parallel VLP developers and priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR and mTOR as the central regulator of growth and nutrient response links cell biology to cancer, immunosuppression, metabolism and ageing. Fundamental and widely consequential.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin target identification was pivotal; Sabatini contributed mTORC1 nutrient sensing but is a more complicated choice. Brown and Sabatini's contributions to mTOR identification are partially captured.
assessment.maturity: Mature, broadly confirmed and extended; rapamycin analogues are in clinical use.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between yeast genetics and mammalian target identification is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: LTP is the leading cellular model for synaptic plasticity underlying learning and memory, with decades of mechanistic work (NMDA receptor dependence). Highly original and conceptually influential for neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo discovered LTP in 1973; Collingridge established NMDA receptor dependence; Morris linked it to spatial learning. Four credited names exceed three slots.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; the causal link between LTP and memory has been tested but remains debated.
uncertainties: Causal role of LTP in memory is still not fully established.
Direct disease or therapeutic impact is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of Lgr5 stem cells and long-term adult stem-cell organoid culture produced a platform used for disease modeling, drug testing and personalized medicine. Wide impact on experimental biology.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led Lgr5 identification and organoid culture with Sato as the key first author; the two-person configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over a decade; clinical translation still emerging.
uncertainties: Tool versus discovery framing and relation to other stem-cell prizes.
Precise attribution to Sato versus others in the Clevers lab is not independently verified.
